items.text: the sticker's frame is a row of color chips, like the color shelf's swatches: none (diagonal lines), white, black and your own color. Press and hold any chip, or tap the last one, to mix a frame color of your own in the Color mixer

what goes under the sticker is "Extras": Brand, Text and QR are toggles, any mix of them, or none. Text writes your own words (the scene's word until you type); the QR opens this scene. They sit in one tidy tab under the sticker

while Capture is on Sticker, a live preview of the sticker floats above the bar, so you change the frame and extras while looking at it. Tap it to make the sticker: it grows into the share sheet, and shrinks back when you close it
the share sheet closes where it opened: its close button sits exactly over the Capture button, so a capture made by mistake is undone by tapping the same spot again
when the sound goes off, the circle grows back into the Sound button a shade darker: the signal is on, the sound is off
the Sound drawer's caret hides while the off thermometer runs and comes back after
the playing Sound button's level wave is dark teal again, as before the thermometer (white didn't read)

a small gear in the corner of each Auto play "Changes" tile takes you to where that thing is made: Pattern to the Pattern tool, Style to Color, Sound to the sound drawer and its beats, Material to Water and the surface, Scene to your scenes. A tap on the gear never switches the tile

the dice can roll at random intervals: the last bead of its "how often" row, a pair of dice, picks each next wait from the row (2, 4, 8, 15, 30 or 60 seconds, or beats or bars), never the same twice running, so it never falls into step with the robot. The bead timing the next roll wears a ring that fills to it
in the Sound drawer, "your file" is now "track" and "instruments" is "kit", so no label is cut off

a change of scene really morphs now. The colors cross over instead of jumping: the lines, the second color, touch, arrows, the pattern, and the ground (the stage and the trails follow it every frame), all in OKLab, so a dark ground warms through its own tones into terracotta

the field morphs too: the old current blends into the new one, so the particles drift from one into the next; the lens dips to nothing and comes back if it changes mode; lines, arrows and the pattern fade out and in
Morph is a row of beads like Every: Cut · 2 · 4 · 8 · 16 · 30 · 60 seconds, 8 by default. Cut is the instant change. The bead timing a morph wears a ring that fills to its end
a scene with its own morph says so at the Morph row's right ("this scene: 2 s"); without one, the row's choice is used. Snap, glide and slow come across as Cut, 2 and 8
a lit button is light again: the accent lifted toward white, a thick accent edge, a dark icon; the Sound button's level wave is white
the off thermometer is one piece: the same light blue fill, one thick accent edge round the bulb and up the neck (the button's thin grey rim steps aside while it runs)
on the lit Sound button the level wave is drawn in the ink (white on dark, black on light), so it stands apart from the accent edge and icon
the off thermometer's outline is the Sound button's own grey rim, carried up the neck; the rim stays visible through the whole drain and fade
the sound's off thermometer is frosted like the lit button it grows from: an accent wash on dark glass with an accent outline and icon, so neck and button match

a lit button on the bar (robot, dice, sound, tools) keeps the frosted glass, warmed with the accent, with an accent edge and icon, so it matches the drawers and shelf it opens; the dice's amount ring is accent again

turning the sound off is a thermometer that grows up out of the Sound button, filled in the button's own colour. The pill drains first while the sound stays full; when the level reaches the button, its fill shrinks and the sound fades with it. Touch any part of it, pill or button, to bring the sound back: it refills and sinks back into the button
